_readme: 12 labeled scenarios. `evidence_bundle` is what the agents actually receive (fixtures/scenarios/*.json). `expected_findings` is what a CORRECTLY functioning agent pair should produce -- hand-derived from the evidence + prompts/*.md rules, not from a live LLM run. `expected` is the scoreRun() output when scorer.js is fed expected_findings -- eval/score_eval.test.js asserts this automatically (it's deterministic code, no LLM needed). During Phase 6, run the REAL agents against each evidence_bundle and diff their actual findings against expected_findings by hand -- that comparison is eval/run_eval.md's job, and it's the one part of this file that genuinely needs a live n8n+Gemini run, see that doc for why.

cases.name: flaky test + unreachable critical CVE (GitHub red, AutoRelease approves)
reachable critical CVE + coverage drop (GitHub green, AutoRelease blocks -- the demo centerpiece)
real regression, suspect commit named
cases.expected_findings_note: two failing tests from the same underlying bug -> two new_regression findings, cap kicks in on the second (see cap test in scoring/scorer.test.js)

cases.name: secret in diff -- BLOCK gate overrides score
cases.note: score/band alone would say approve -- decision must still be block. This is the single most important row in this table to get right.

cases.name: variant: flaky test that has now become a genuine regression (same test, but this run's failure is NOT in its historical pattern)
cases.note: Build during Phase 6: same test as test_flaky.py but failing on a run_number NOT divisible by 3 (i.e. off-pattern) -- tests whether the agent correctly distinguishes 'matches known flake pattern' from 'coincidentally the same test, different cause'. Genuinely hard case -- expect confidence:medium, not high.

cases.name: variant: import without any symbol usage anywhere (fully unused dependency)
cases.note: Build during Phase 6: a Dependabot alert for a package NOT imported anywhere -- tests the 'not imported at all' branch of prompts/security_agent.md's reachability rule, separate from S2/S3's 'imported but function unused' case.

cases.name: variant: infra timeout (runner network failure, not a code issue)
cases.note: Build during Phase 6: a job log containing a network/timeout-shaped error, no assertion failure -- tests infra_failure classification, 0 score impact by design.

cases.name: variant: agent output fails validation twice -> synthetic low-confidence finding, forced manual review
cases.note: Simulate during Phase 6 by forcing a schema-invalid agent response twice (e.g. temporarily break the output parser) and confirming validation/validateFinding.js's syntheticLowConfidenceFinding() fires and routes correctly -- this proves the 'never fail silently into an approval' rule actually holds.

cases.name: variant: reachable critical CVE with low confidence (import-level only, no function list)
cases.note: Build during Phase 6: a CVE whose advisory lists no vulnerable_functions and has no vulnerable_functions.json fallback entry -- tests prompts/security_agent.md step 4 (default reachable, confidence medium, NOT low -- so this should NOT trigger manual_review; contrast with V4).

cases.name: variant: multiple flaky tests hit the cap
cases.note: Already covered end-to-end in scoring/scorer.test.js ('flaky_test cap' test) -- listed here for completeness of the 12-case table judges may ask to see, not because it needs a fresh evidence bundle.

cases.name: variant: code_scanning_alert unrelated to any CVE (pure CodeQL quality/security-pattern finding)
cases.note: Build during Phase 6: a CodeQL alert not tied to a Dependabot package (e.g. a SQL-injection-shaped pattern alert) -- tests the code_scanning_alert category path distinct from secret_detected and the CVE categories.
